📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the first time since 2014, Sacramento Republic are USL Champions. Republic defeated Louisville City FC in a penalty shootout following a 1-1 draw Saturday at Heart Health Park, capturing the club's second title and extending its unbeaten run to 17 matches.

In a final between two of the best teams in USL history, it had to have been the narrowest of margins that settled the outcome, with each goalkeeper making a save during the shootout before Sacramento eventually prevailed in front of its home fans.

RYAN SPAULDING HAS WON THE USL CHAMPIONSHIP TITLE FOR @SacRepublicFC‼️😤#USLonCBS | @bestwestern pic.twitter.com/OeFARGXyyh.

The second star comes at a symbolic moment for Sacramento Republic, which is preparing to move from Heart Health Park and into a new 20,000-seat soccer-specific venue in the Railyards district of downtown Sacramento in 2028. The emotions were evident on the faces of Louisville City players after the loss as they came to terms with what happened.

Despite an early start to the USL Cup final in Sacramento, with kickoff at 9 a.m. local time, there was no need to wait for goals, as Louisville and Sacramento both scored within the opening 32 minutes. Cal Jennings struck in the 14th minute, while Ray Serrano answered in the 31st.

It was then the defenses that took the reins to calm the game down as Sacramento held possession to control a dangerous Louisville attack, and when Evan Davila's shootout attempt hit the post, it opened the door for Sacramento keeper Danny Vitiello to win it, and that he did.

An evenly matched final was exactly what many expected, and it delivered for Sacramento fans, who started tailgating at 5:30 a.m. and brought the energy from start to finish. Neil Collins' experienced side looked prepared for the moment, and had Mark-Anthony Kaye's effort not struck the post, Sacramento may have settled the match in regulation. Instead, it required a shootout, and that's where Republic ultimately got the job done.

It has been revealed that A moment @SacRepublicFC will never forget 🏆✨Catch the full trophy presentation on CBS Sports! 📺➡️ https://t.co/5eh4N4wm1X pic.twitter.com/ESzeWP0IgO.

On the Louisville side, despite winning the Prinx Tires Cup during the regular season, they've now failed to win the final in three appearances since their last triumph in 2018. Considering their regular-season success, they'll want to get over the hump, but given how consistent they've been, it's impossible to say they won't be back at this stage next season.

Man City will be hoping to close the gap on Arsenal to three points at the top of the table after the north London side’s 1-0 win over Hull City this afternoon.

While matters off the pitch may suggest otherwise, on it, City look the most likely side to deny Mikel Arteta’s men a second successive league title.

Forest are yet to score at home in any competition this season and have netted only six league goals in total from an xG of 14.34.

That underperformance of 8.34 goals is the biggest of any team in the Premier League this season, and of any side after nine Premier League games since at least 2021-22.

Forest come into this evening’s game in 19th, but they are just a point behind Crystal Palace and Manchester United, while victory would also take them above Coventry City and up to 16th.

Forest’s results at the City Ground have to improve swiftly or this team will be in serious trouble.

They have gone almost eight and a half hours without scoring in front of their own supporters.

Forest have only recorded two home wins in the Premier League over the past 11 months which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

Oliver Glasner has played down the significance of his warning to Nottingham Forest’s squad after their defeat at Brentford has had the desired impact.

The Austrian remarked last weekend there would be “no compromises” and insisted his players have to fully buy into his philosophy.

Speaking this week, he said: “I didn’t attack anyone directly. We share that we want to be successful and win games. It was not a problem.

According to recent reports, “It was much louder outside than I felt it was inside. This is just how I see a relationship has to be. Let’s talk about things if we don’t like things.

“If you never say anything in your relationship with your wife or children, then they will never know. Then I can’t blame somebody because if they don’t know, how can you expect things to change?

“We are now in a society where criticism or the way I talk is negative, but the intention was positive and to change to get better results so that we can all have a better life.”.

Gianluigi Donnarumma, who has made three errors leading to goals this season, “recognises that he has made some mistakes,” Enzo Maresca remarked this week, “but at the same time recognises that he has made some great saves”.

The City manager added: “It is quite easy with him because he recognises any mistake immediately. I’ve spoken to him about it, but I didn’t feel the need to be so deep with him because he already knows and recognises that he has made some mistakes.”.

Asked about City players adapting to his philosophy, Maresca remarked: “I can see my playing style just by working every day with them, but we can still improve many things.

“We know exactly what we are doing well and what we need to improve. It is just a matter of time.”.

Elsewhere this afternoon, Martin Odegaard has broken the deadlock at the Emirates to give Arsenal a 1-0 lead over Hull City.

Victory would take Mikel Arteta’s side six points clear of City at the top of the table before this evening’s contest at the City Ground.

Is this the day the xG gods reward Nottingham Forest? Oliver Glasner’s team sit 19th having won one game all season, but there is no doubt that their performances have been significantly better than results and they might need their luck to turn against Man City team full of firepower.

Despite all of the positive indicators in Forest’s underlying data, Glasner caused some alarm with his comments after last weekend’s defeat at Brentford.

The Austrian remarked: “We have to accept it’s not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it’s not good enough. And that’s why for me, it’s now time that we change things, that I change things, and that’s what I will do.

“I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it’s always compromises. It’s a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in.”.

Dangerous words perhaps when you work for Evangelos Marinakis, but John Percy reported this week that Glasner was backed by his players in a squad meeting.

According to recent reports, city are smarting from back-to-back defeats by Aston Villa and Brighton, but they created more than enough in both games to claim some sort of result. Nevertheless, there is a persistent sense that their defensive unit remains too marshmellow-like over the course of 38 games, and Forest have the counter-attacking threat to test them.

Glasner has happy memories of playing City, beating them in the 2025 FA Cup final with Crystal Palace, but his Forest reign is in urgent need of a signature victory and performance.

HENRY WINTER: Bruno Fernandes has been a brilliant servant, but it's time to cut the cord at Manchester United

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (888 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United are under newly introduced management and need to be under new leadership on the field.
  • It has been revealed that bruno Fernandes has undeniably been a flickering beacon of brief hope for United in darkening times.
  • Sources indicate that even taking up the year’s option (unless to increase the player’s transfer fee) would be a retrograde step.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United are under newly introduced management and need to be under new leadership on the field.

It has been revealed that bruno Fernandes has undeniably been a flickering beacon of brief hope for United in darkening times. He’s been their Player of the Year in five of the last seven seasons, risen to 19th of their greatest scorers with 113 goals, has scored 75 times (24 pens, four free-kicks) and provided 74 assists in 240 Premier League games and is the reigning Footballer of the Year. But it’s undeniably time for the club to face reality, resist the urge to extend a contract which expires next summer and build for the future.

Sources indicate that even taking up the year’s option (unless to increase the player’s transfer fee) would be a retrograde step. Fernandes is 32, slowing up, and not now “best in class, 10 out of 10s” to borrow Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s catchphrase. He is not the most convincing of captains, moans too much and flaps his arms like a fledgling dove attempting to leave the nest.

Fernandes would never, ever be considered one of United’s elite captains in a strong, historic field that includes Sir Bobby Charlton, Roy Keane, Bryan Robson, Steve Bruce, Roger Byrne, Nemanja Vidic and Gary Neville, amongst others.

All are different; Neville was very vocal, Charlton led by example, but were united in their total commitment.

In a recent development, fernandes’ leadership qualities were brought into question when he openly criticised the tactics of Michael Carrick, effectively undermining him. That may not have been Fernandes’ intention when questioning the tactical approach against Como but it certainly didn’t help Carrick at a time when he needed players standing up to be counted, not standing up to his tactics in public. Such concerns – some of them legitimate – should have been aired in private.

Industry observers note that it showed a lack of leadership from Fernandes, a lack of gratitude, too. Fernandes wouldn’t have been named the writers’ Footballer of the Year and the players’ Player of the Year without Carrick reviving United’s fortunes and their No. 8’s form last season.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In receiving the writers’ award in May, Fernandes eulogised about the interim head coach, praising “the amazing job” he did in guiding United into the Champions League and saying Carrick possesses the “great character to become a top manager”.

Such an endorsement from such an influential figure at the club, effectively the voice of the dressing-room, undoubtedly contributed to Ineos and the Glazers appointing Carrick to the permanent role.

According to recent reports, bruno’s voice is powerful. That is why it was damaging when he spoke out against Carrick’s tactics. “Lies,” was Bruno’s reaction to some of the interpretation of his words but mud stuck.

Carrick questioned individuals’ running stats – without naming Fernandes – and then dropped him for the game against Bournemouth. United need real leaders. In fairness to Fernandes, there are plenty of stories of the good work he does behind the scenes.

Who would inherit the armband in the unlikely event that Carrick’s successor, Mauricio Pochettino, was brave and looked to the future? Matthijs de Ligt, an Ajax captain at 18, would be a strong contender were it not for his back problems. Senne Lammens represents United admirably on and off the field, and was one of only two who emerged with reputation intact from Anfield.

The other was Kobbie Mainoo. It might seem a leap of faith in one so young, still only 21, but Mainoo could perform the duties until a more experienced leader was recruited by the club that once bought Keane, Bruce, Vidic etc. (All of this is a reminder of United’s need to buy leaders, powerful characters as well as good players).

In a recent development, mainoo’s one of the few deserving of his place at the moment. He’s also an academy graduate, a local lad, and a link to great home-grown generations. Fans would love that re-affirmation of United’s identity. It would be quite a statement by Pochettino.

Mainoo has only minimal captaincy experience against Bayern Munich in 2017 (as a kid) and successfully with England Under-19s in 2023. More recently, more pertinently, Mainoo acted like a leader against Roma on November 3 when others were losing their discipline.

It’s still too early, of course, and Mainoo is still developing but he could do the honours on a temporary basis in the unlikely event that United cut the cord with Fernandes. But a recruitment department incapable of making strong decisions and buying “best in class” – they were not in the running when Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers were available in the summer - may be tempted to go for the easy option of keeping Fernandes, rather than step into a newly introduced era.

Henry Winter is one of football's most popular and respected writers. Previously the Chief Football Writer for The Times and a Football Correspondent for The Daily Telegraph, his work now primarily features on his Substack. He has also lauched his own podcast 'The Winter View'.

Science’s greatest failure is not getting things wrong, but by sometimes pretending that there is more certainty than there really is, indicates social scientist Andy Stirling.

This can happen, he says, when researchers face political pressure to provide a single, definitive answer, when the evidence is far more complex.

In the final episode of a six-part podcast series about failure in science, Stirling, an emeritus professor at the University of Sussex in Brighton, UK, draws on examples from climate change, the COVID-19 pandemic, environmental campaigns and energy policy.

Sources indicate that “In those areas, science just does not convey the degree of uncertainty and of variability and of how many potentially viable options are being cut out when you just give one clear answer,” he says. “It thinks it’s helping society by just giving one picture of the truth. And in fact, it’s undermining both itself and democracy when it does that.”.

Stirling, whose research includes science and technology policy and environmental politics, claims that on occasions politicians have almost literally hidden behind scientists on a podium, who have relied on their authority and expertise to protect them.

Earlier this year, Stirling spoke at a one-day conference on failure in science, with a focus on careers and innovation. It was held at Imperial College London in partnership with Nature.

So COVID is an example of this. I think we had to pretend there was one policy because it was so stressful.

Politicians had to pretend because otherwise they would have to hide behind their chief scientists, literally sometimes, literally behind them on the podium, hiding behind them because they needed that authority to protect them from the inevitable uncertainties that everyone believed were really there, even though they weren’t acknowledging it in the graphs.

I mean, blame management, trust, public acceptance.

These things are the most notable commodities in politics. So yeah, and it’s you know apocryphally, people have all kinds of anecdotes out on these advisory committees.

I’ve served a little bit on some of them. You know, the number of times in which the politicians will intimate, "I won’t hesitate to hide behind you," almost as a joke.

But so you know, scientists respond to that in different ways. But by and large, they think, "Well, okay, we’ve got to be responsible. Let’s give these guys a single prescriptive answer, even though we know among ourselves that we could have got a different answer, but we’ve got a responsibility not to do an to do to do an elevator pitch.".

You know, not to give on the one hand, on the other, as Margaret Thatcher remarked, "Save me from the two-handed economist. I want a one-handed economist.".

Recent findings suggest that she wants it because of justification, but actually, it’s a responsibility of the economist, or in this case, a scientist, to actually explain how it does depend. It always does depend.

If they don’t explain that, then they are failing, I would say science, and failing society, failing democracy.

Industry observers note that other things are really complicated. there’s a lot of real challenges. I don’t want to pretend it’s easier than it really is.

Industry observers note that but actually, we shouldn’t be paralyzed by this. Look at science itself. When it developed in the 17th century, motto of the Royal Society, nullius in verba, that was basically saying that principles of accountability, of argument, of deliberation really mattered, of treating people more equally than many institutions do. That’s not the opposite of democracy. That is democracy.

Science was about, in many ways, democratizing knowledge.

Sources indicate that you know, you needed to argue, you need to show evidence and do analyzes in rigorous ways. But it should be open to anyone to do that, and to any perspective, no matter how ridiculous it sounds, if it can substantiate itself.

So science and democracy are not on opposite sides.

So I think, rather than counterpointing them, like science is against democracy, we can’t trust democracy, going to undermine science, actually, see it the other way round: that science is an embodiment of democracy.

It’s when it is at its best. It’s when it’s being democratic about the ability to challenge power inside science, and that’s how we solve the problems of science.

It’s also how we solve the problems at the moment of democracy, which science is, sadly, because it’s forced to be more authoritarian in pretending a singular truth.

It’s forced into that not by democracy, but by power that is also eroding democracy.

So I think the answer is democracy.

Science, when it comes to advise policymakers, yes, please do your best, but don’t think of yourself just giving a single expedient answer so that a politician goes away happy and can act without worrying about blame.

Inform society at large about the assumptions that went into that.

Show how it depends, and if you do that, you’re informing democracy as much as the powerful actors who are, you know, maybe conferring the patronage on the scientists.

Science fails when it’s not being plural enough.

It needs to be plural about who’s involved, about the questions that are asked, about the disciplines that get around the table, about how it conveys its interpretations of its understandings out to society, and it needs to just not be scared of representing that plurality because with that comes the conditions.

Industry observers note that it’s not just anything goes. It’s not plural for plurality’s sake.

It’s then saying under what conditions you get answer X or answer Y, and that’s more scientific.

It’s more rigorous to behave in that way.

When science does that, it’s being more scientific when it’s plural. So I think science fails most when it reduces all those kinds of plurality.

To just a singular idea of truth.

#208929. What has changed in James Bond films over the decades

What has changed in James Bond films over the decades

📅 05 Oct 2022 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1185 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After years of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday that Robert Pattinson would be taking on the role of James Bond following Daniel Craig's departure after five hit films in the spy series.
  • This year alone, Pattinson has starred in "The Odyssey," "The Drama" and "Primetime." He is also famous for his role as "Twilight" vampire Edward Cullen.
  • The upcoming Bond movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, an Oscar nominee known for movies such as the "Dune" trilogy and "Arrival.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After years of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday that Robert Pattinson would be taking on the role of James Bond following Daniel Craig's departure after five hit films in the spy series.

This year alone, Pattinson has starred in "The Odyssey," "The Drama" and "Primetime." He is also famous for his role as "Twilight" vampire Edward Cullen.

The upcoming Bond movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, an Oscar nominee known for movies such as the "Dune" trilogy and "Arrival.".

Based on the spy novels by author Ian Fleming, the Bond franchise — about a British secret agent known for his charm and ⁠a ⁠fondness for martinis "shaken, not stirred" — is among the longest-running and highest-grossing in Hollywood history. ​​​​​​​.

The first film in the series, "Dr. No," premiered in London on October 5, 1962.

Playing the leading role, Agent 007, was an unknown actor: Sean Connery.

Industry observers note that in the film, we are first introduced to his character as he sits in a casino across from an attractive woman who is about to gamble away her fortune. When she asks 007 his name, the camera pans to Bond lighting a cigarette. With a smoldering look in his eye, he utters the legendary words: "Bond, James Bond.".

Sources indicate that shortly thereafter in the film, 007 receives an assignment to fly to Jamaica and investigate the murder of another M16 agent. He eventually tracks down a Chinese-German criminal scientist who is bent on destroying the US space program and achieving world domination.

According to recent reports, in principle, this story is the basis of all of 25 James Bond films. Whether the villain is Dr. No, Blofeld, Goldfinger or Le Chiffre, they all aim for one thing: world domination. But to do so, they have to get past James Bond whose gunfire and wild chase scenes inevitably spoil their aims.

In a recent development, although many fan forums consider "Dr. No" to be one of the best Bond films, the movie would never be made in the same way today.

Firstly, one could write entire books about the omnipresent sexism and machismo that the character James Bond has displayed over the decades.

Certainly there would have to be a thick chapter dedicated to the women in his films, who are typically portrayed as naive, willingly flinging themselves into Bond's arms, seeking protection. Sometimes they are sophisticated female antagonists who lose control at the thought of hopping into bed with the secret agent.

Recent findings suggest that whether friend of foe, each film had at least one Bond girl — and often more: More than 60 love interests have appeared in the films. Their names, like "Honey" or "Pussy Galore" would never be acceptable today. In more recent decades, female roles in Bond films have changed — as has Bond himself.

In the last five films in which Daniel Craig has played Bond, he is seen as a man who is tough on the outside and soft on the inside — and who is not always lucky with women.

Aside from the portrayal of women on screen, there are also plenty of other details in "Dr. No" that haven't quite stood the test of time.

Recent findings suggest that another sign of the zeitgeist in the 1962 film is that everyone smokes, which is a no-no by today's Hollywood standards. Cigarettes are found everywhere in the old film, from the casino to the hotel bar — and even the bedroom.

It has been revealed that smoking was commonplace in the US in the 1970s, so naturally this came across on the silver screen. In the 1970s TV series "Space: 1999" people were even depicted smoking on the moon, but by the 2000s, smoking was largely banned in many parts of the world due to its health risks.

It has been revealed that one can also note in "Dr. No" that few people are wearing seat belts. When Bond drives off in his sports car to visit a woman, he is followed and a chase scene ensues. Bond, notably, is not wearing a seat belt.

His pursuers eventually drive off a slope and die, of course — after all, they aren't wearing seat belts either and cars didn't have airbags at the time. The vehicle explodes, prompting 007 to say, "They were obviously in a hurry to get to their own funeral.".

In the older Bond films, all secretaries and receptionists are played by women, which in the 1960s, were considered standard female jobs.

Whether redheaded, blonde or brunette, secretaries are Bond's favorite targets for womanizing and they are all susceptible to his charms.

Throughout most Bond films, the agent has a romantic tension with Moneypenny, his boss's secretary, something which was not described in the original books.

According to recent reports, in the 2012 film "Skyfall" Moneypenny is given a first name: Eve, and we finally learn her backstory. In this film, she is no longer a hopeless secretary in love, but a top-trained agent who accidentally shoots Bond and is reassigned to desk duty as punishment.

In any case, today Moneypenny's job title today would probably be "Office Manager" or "Executive Assistant" rather than "Secretary.".

Industry observers note that in the film, Dr. No tells James Bond that he is the child of a British missionary and a Chinese woman from an upstanding family. However, the character is portrayed by Canadian actor Joseph Wiseman who is wearing makeup to make his eyes look more "Asian.".

While it used to be the norm in such movies to have East Asian characters played by white actors, today these cases of "yellowface" are frowned upon — just as it would be to wear blackface, putting black makeup on one's skin to portray a Black person.

In a recent development, if there was a "Dr. No" remake in the future, a Chinese actor would be more likely to play this role.

Daniel Craig already paved the way in modernizing James Bond by stripping away campy gadgets, punchlines and invincibility, replacing them with a grounded, psychological and emotionally vulnerable portrayal of a post-9/11 spy.

It has been revealed that now it is up to Robert Pattinson to revisit the famous MI6 agent. Film critics believe his background will allow him to add dark sophistication and nonconformism to the iconic espionage role.

Throughout his career, Robert Pattinson has managed to combine roles in blockbuster hits and indie gems, from Bruce Wayne in "The Batman" to a disposable worker who is cloned every time he dies in "Mickey 17.".

Pattinson already has experience with classic spy archetypes: As the mysterious Neil in Christopher Nolan's sci-fi action thriller "Tenet," he assisted the protagonist in a time-bending espionage mission. He is also known for his eccentric personality and deadpan humor — qualities that could be useful for a modern Bond.

It has been revealed that this article was translated from German by Sarah Hucal. It was first published in 2025 and updated following news of Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond on November 16, 2026.

#208927. Vlatko Andonovski built it, Chris Armas finished it: KC Current's NWSL title was continuity through disruption

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1452 w)
📖 Baca

Vlatko Andonovski built it, Chris Armas finished it: KC Current's NWSL title was continuity through disruption

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1452 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • – The Kansas City Current were built to experience a confetti shower, one they undoubtedly felt was not a moment too soon, even if it came a year later than expected.
  • It has been revealed that there was a trademark sense of inevitability that usually follows a team en route to victory, the Current dictating the game state and never looking back against the Spirit.
  • Sources indicate that there was a disruptive quality to their run to the championship, one that is inherently rooted in a decision to distance the architect of the project from the project itself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WASHINGTON, D.C. – The Kansas City Current were built to experience a confetti shower, one they undoubtedly felt was not a moment too soon, even if it came a year later than expected. It is hard not to view their first-ever NWSL Championship, which came via a 2-1 win over the Washington Spirit on Saturday, as a continuation of last year's record-breaking Shield triumph and their consistency in recent years, boasting the most cumulative points out of any team in the last three seasons.

It has been revealed that there was a trademark sense of inevitability that usually follows a team en route to victory, the Current dictating the game state and never looking back against the Spirit. This, though, was not a year of continuity for the Current.

Sources indicate that there was a disruptive quality to their run to the championship, one that is inherently rooted in a decision to distance the architect of the project from the project itself. Chris Armas inherited a team built by Vlatko Andonovski, who first shifted to a sporting director role at the start of the season and then abruptly left in late summer in a move that inspired a wave of emotions from a squad that started to look like a title contender when Andonovski took charge in 2024. Armas began to work with a team that was already capable of winning a title and will be credited with seeing the vision through, all while putting his own spin on things. He also inherited a perfect set of circumstances, which ultimately got the Current over the finish line.

Recent findings suggest that "I walked into a really good team," Armas said post-match. "There was a good culture built in. There was a lot of good pieces and that was one of the reasons that lured me to the club … My job as the head coach is just to try to assess the situation and through tough times help us be steady.".

The Current won eight straight games to close out the season, a run in which they were at their best because they were at their strongest. Their championship-winning season can ultimately be split in two – the stretch of the season in which Temwa Chawinga, Michelle Cooper and Croix Bethune were all fit and available and the stretch of the season in which at least one was missing. It is understandable that the Current would rely on a trio like that one, especially as Bethune became a finishing touch of sorts when she arrived last winter. By design, the group was always going to bolster the Current's chances of going the distance.

"I'm relying on these amazing people and players to help keep things steady but we have talent all along," Armas continued. "We just had to get everyone back and healthy and then we knew we'd have a chance. The question would be, would we have enough time? And we had time, and they did the rest. We stayed steady. We have a great team and we peaked at the right time and now they're champions.".

In a recent development, their overreliance on them, though, did not matter when the business end of the season came. The Current's starry trio was ready; by default, so were the Current.

In a recent development, armas' team is distinct from Andonovski's in several ways, as evidenced in the NWSL's most glittery moment of the season. Vanessa DiBernardo's olimpico opened the scoring in the second half was the most stylish way of the Current's increased emphasis on set pieces since Armas took over, a skill that was also incredibly useful in their semifinal win at Gotham FC.

Sources indicate that VANESSA DIBERNARDO SCORES AN OLIMPICO IN THE NWSL CHAMPIONSHIP TO PUT KC CURRENT IN FRONT 🤯Stream all the @nwsl championship action on @cbs and @paramountplus. pic.twitter.com/dcZTivEoNt.

"Lucas Rodriguez has been here from the literal day one," captain Lo'eau LaBonta said about set piece coach Lucas Rodriguez. "We have been talking about it for the last couple weeks, where we started and where we are now and, so, also that first year, it was his first time ever in women's soccer, so he's grown with the game as well, and he's learned the league and I think that's absolutely what helped him create these amazing set pieces to help us win the trophy.".

According to recent reports, the vestiges of Andonovski's team, though, are hard to miss. The journey that led them to Saturday's win was essentially a direct response to the NWSL Shield win that Andonovski oversaw a year ago, a race that was complete by the end of September, a whole month between their trophy lift and their 2025 quarterfinal defeat to Gotham.

"I think we needed to lose in those quarters almost to lift the trophy and win it all this year because it was just different," captain Lo'eau LaBonta remarked. "We won the Shield so early last year that we never really had that playoff mentality going into the playoffs because we had already been in it for so long so now that we've experienced everything on each side, I think we absolutely are going to use this to hopefully get help us going forward and make a legacy.".

Industry observers note that it is not a pattern that is unfamiliar in Armas' career, either. Saturday's championship is the first major title he collected as a coach since 2018, when he led MLS' New York Red Bulls to the Supporters' Shield. Though he was an assistant for several years in the build-up, he also inherited that team from Jesse Marsch, who left midseason for the start of an up-and-down coaching stint in Europe that began at Red Bull Salzburg. The success became hard to replicate; the Red Bulls finished sixth in 2019 and again in 2020, though Armas was out of a job before the season was up. He only managed a few months at Toronto FC, had his own adventures as an assistant coach in England with Ralf Rangnick's Manchester United and at the end of Marsch's ill-fated spell at Leeds United, and then led the Colorado Rapids to a seventh-place finish in 2024 and missed the playoffs in 2025.

Recent findings suggest that armas' Current exist in a fascinating in-between when it comes to the mold of championship-winning teams. They created a game state that rattled the Spirit from start to finish for the most part, notably doing so while staying true to the attacking identity Andonovski established. The key was creating a physical game state, one that they trialed at Gotham a week earlier and then turned the dial up on at the Spirit on Saturday. The plan worked – they limited the Spirit to just 0.77 expected goals from 18 shots, all while generating 2.32 from their 15.

"We are a physical team and there was a lot of whistles and a kind of disruptive play but at the end of the day, we do want to be disruptors so it doesn't matter," defender Kayla Sharples said. "We're going to keep that aggression. I think that's what we did and so we tried not to let it faze us. If anything, it kind of got us more hyped. We need to stay focused and have that mentality finishing off the game.".

There's also the belief that championship-winning teams are often defined by their ability to survive in imperfect circumstances. Their record with and without their starry trio indicates one thing but with winners' medals around their necks, the Current's players believe they managed to strike the best of both worlds approach in order to win on Saturday. Time will tell if Armas can actually extend his streak, something he was unable to do at the Red Bulls. There were undoubtedly moments of adversity along the way, though, their playoff hopes far from a guarantee with five games left in the regular season and a consistency that at least resembles the 2025 Shield-winning campaign will be key in 2027.

Industry observers note that "We kind of have the same style of play but I think Chris has done a great job being the fuel and the fire, making sure we're emphasizing certain details," Sharples said. "I think what we went through this year, where we learned a lot about resiliency and grit and we were down goals, we went and we came back to win and that's what you need in order to be successful at the end of the season, so I think that was, honestly, the massive takeaway from the season, and it really helped us at the end of the day.".

Crystal Palace are playing this season as if afflicted by a curse. They seem to have made a terrible deal, possibly involving a monkey’s paw. As a result, Pierre Sage’s team were able to defend credibly for around 44 minutes of each half, on one condition: They must switch off completely, at least twice per game.

According to recent reports, this being the Premier League, those lapses in concentration are usually punished. A mostly compact performance out of possession briefly became as porous as a bath sponge when Liverpool eased into a 2-0 lead, nine minutes after half-time. Florian Wirtz did not even need to finish cleanly to score his first Premier League goal of the season, striding on to an unopposed low cross from Bradley Barcola and killing the match as a contest.

Industry observers note that bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz combine to put Liverpool 2-0 up! 🔴 https://t.co/F6sw33FkYZ.

Major signings need to lay down a marker when arriving at Liverpool. Barcola has his hat-trick at LASK in the Champions League, but we are still waiting for a stirring major-match-defining contribution from him since his summer arrival. Arguably the same could be noted for Wirtz, nearly 18 months since he joined.

Neither left Selhurst Park looking like the world-beaters they did occasionally for their previous clubs. Still, one misfiring attacker creating a goal for another represents progress and all great partnerships must start somewhere. Lennon and McCartney would improve after 1958’s Too Bad About Sorrows.

If there was ever a place for the least-productive expensively assembled attacking group in the league to find form it was surely south London on this Sunday lunchtime. Liverpool came in with two defeats in their previous two but, European trophy aside, it has been a lousy 2026 for Palace.

They have the most defeats of any ever-present Premier League team and began (and ended) the weekend with the worst defensive record. They have conceded twice as many goals from headers as any other team. Even their most loyal fan group has disbanded.

Sources indicate that alexis Mac Allister opened the scoring in gut-punching fashion, after a series of Palace near-misses. Chairman Steve Parish rubbed his face in the directors’ box, in the style of peak-stress era Guardiola. None of this looked good for Sage, who appears on the brink of dismissal, with Thomas Frank his most likely replacement.

Asked if he expected to remain in his job on the other side of the international break Sage mentioned he deemed his prospects “better than you, I think”.

“We deserved better today,” the Frenchman said. “But football is not about what you deserve it is about how efficient you are and today we had a lack of efficiency”.

Counter-intuitively, it was Palace’s flashes of promise which suggested the Frenchman might be doomed. There is enough to work with here, and plenty going marginally against Palace to suggest a change in leadership might prompt a turnaround, however unfair it would be on their manager. Yéremy Pino hit the bar, Jorgen Strand Larsen had his composed close-range goal struck from the record by VAR, Daichi Kamada stung Alisson Becker’s palms and the Brazilian saved well again from Adam Wharton’s feathered header.

The other factor which seems likely to condemn Sage is his team’s boneheaded defensive lapses. Liverpool were awarded a debatable free-kick out wide, Quinten Timber let Mac Allister run off him too easily and he duly nodded Dominik Szoboszlai’s delivery past Dean Henderson with ease. Another header conceded.

“Happy for him,” Iraola remarked of Wirtz, also praising Isak’s movement for the German’s goal. “I think [Wirtz] has been very unlucky in the Premier League, a couple of goals disallowed and situations where he deserves honestly to score.”.

#208916. How Emile Heskey fell into a sketchy world peddling controversial drugs: From England star worth £12m to bankruptcy, unpaid tax and a bitter divorce

How Emile Heskey fell into a sketchy world peddling controversial drugs: From England star worth £12m to bankruptcy, unpaid tax and a bitter divorce

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1895 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 07:35 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • Emile Heskey is standing in a warehouse, dressed in a black adidas tracksuit, trying to sell you a jar of curious sweet treats.
  • He smiles into the camera with the gentle-giant warmth that characterised his football career – but Heskey is in unfamiliar territory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 07:35 EST, 26 November 2026.

Emile Heskey is standing in a warehouse, dressed in a black adidas tracksuit, trying to sell you a jar of curious sweet treats.

He smiles into the camera with the gentle-giant warmth that characterised his football career – but Heskey is in unfamiliar territory.

Behind him, stacked on shelf after shelf, are containers full of Supreme CBD gummies.

The man who scored in England's 5-1 thrashing of Germany in 2001, who scored 110 Premier League goals for Leicester, Liverpool, Birmingham, Wigan and Aston Villa plus seven more for his country, is, remarkably, trying to flog you an assortment of products containing cannabidiol, a legal but controversial ingredient derived from cannabis.

In a recent development, today, he is promoting a tub of CBD strawberry gummies, as well as oil. If you fancy an exclusive discount, there's a special code bearing his name.

‘I swear by these products for my sleep,’ he writes in the caption on Instagram. ‘They have been fantastic for me for years now!’.

Emile Heskey spends his days trying to flog controversial Supreme CBD products (Instagram: theemileheskey).

He is one of multiple former footballers promoting the products for ex-Olympic boxer Anthony Fowler - despite their illegal claims about the supposed health benefits.

It has been revealed that heskey, 48, was once one of English football's most respected players. He won 62 caps for England, appearing at two World Cups. He won five trophies at Liverpool and two League Cups at Leicester.

According to recent reports, occasionally mocked for his lack of goals – he averaged roughly one every five games during his club career – he carried himself with humour and grace. Since retiring, his reputation has helped him secure roles with England's youth pathway and Leicester's women's team, as well as occasional punditry work for the BBC.

In September, he scored in an England legends match against Poland, playing alongside John Terry and Robbie Fowler. This month, he was a guest of honour at Liverpool's Anfield VIP Experience. He remains a regular on the speakers' circuit, with more appearances booked before Christmas.

It has been revealed that all of which begs the question: what is he doing promoting Supreme CBD? Why is he filming several videos a month for a manufacturer with such a troubled regulatory record?

Where once he shared a dressing room with Steven Gerrard and David Beckham, he now shares an ambassadorial roster with Katie Price.

It is unclear whether Heskey is aware of the concerns surrounding Supreme CBD products, or the repeated occasions on which the company has fallen foul of advertising rules.

Its founder, Anthony Fowler, a former Team GB Olympic boxer, has made unsubstantiated claims that his cannabidiol products can help treat mental health conditions and autism in children.

There is likely a financial incentive for Heskey, although the terms of any arrangement are unclear. Equally, he appears genuinely convinced of the products' benefits. He claims the oil has done wonders for his sleep and eased his aches and pains.

Heskey's wife Chantelle has issued divorce proceedings - and claims he cancelled a holiday with their kids to go away with his new partner instead.

Heskey and his new partner Jade Slusarczyk spent two weeks together in Cyprus and Greece.

Chantelle branded Heskey 'vile' and claimed he deleted her comment on an Instagram post about the new couple's holiday.

Sources indicate that that may well be true. The NHS acknowledges that CBD has some medical uses, but warns that the ‘quality and content’ of products sold online can be uncertain and that they ‘may be illegal and potentially dangerous’. Nor is there any guarantee that products sold in health stores will be of ‘good quality’.

According to recent reports, supreme CBD have repeatedly breached advertising rules. In June, the Advertising Standards Authority took action over the manufacturer's continued use of prohibited claims that CBD could treat, prevent or cure human disease.

The regulator has also upheld complaints about celebrity promotions that failed to make clear they were advertisements.

Supreme CBD have made claims that their products can treat anxiety, insomnia and depression. Such medicinal claims are prohibited in advertising for products that have not been authorised as medicines. It is uncomfortable ground for Heskey to find himself on.

Last year, Fowler also spoke about refusing chemotherapy for his two-year-old daughter's tumour, claiming CBD oil had had a 'massive' effect on it instead. Price, a paid brand ambassador, amplified those claims on her own social media channels, including posted to her 1.6million followers on X that the tumour had 'shrunk' as a result.

British medical and food safety authorities advise that CBD should not be given to those under the age of 18.

According to recent reports, CBD can also affect how other medicines work, meaning anyone using it alongside other treatments should seek medical advice. Certain medicinal CBD treatments require regular monitoring because of their potential effects on the liver.

In a recent development, it is not unusual for former sportspeople to struggle with insomnia, depression or persistent pain after retirement. In a digital world where anyone can extol the virtues of a product to thousands of followers, it is perhaps unsurprising that cannabis oil has attracted so much attention. Some customers say it has helped them.

Heskey celebrates with David Beckham after scoring for England against Denmark at the 2002 World Cup.

Many of Heskey's almost 100,000 Instagram followers appear equally enthusiastic, with comments beneath his posts endorsing the benefits he describes.

And Heskey is hardly alone among former footballers. Supreme CBD products have also been endorsed by former Arsenal and England playmaker Paul Merson – who has his name on a bundle of his 'favourite' products available to buy on the company's website – Heskey's old Liverpool team-mate Chris Kirkland, Southampton hero Matt Le Tissier and ex-Nottingham Forest goalkeeper Mark Crossley, while ex-Liverpool striker John Aldridge has insisted the product was ‘good for me’.

Life after football has, at times, been rather messy for Heskey.

In a recent development, in 2009, his wealth was estimated at £12million. He had built a clean-cut image and maintained a relatively low profile away from the pitch. Yet just a year later, in 2010, he was declared bankrupt.

Recent findings suggest that his subsequent business dealings have brought further difficulties. Earlier this year, Heskey became caught up in a legal dispute surrounding an allegedly fraudulent £15m takeover of Cypriot club Apollon Limassol by British businessman Craig Gabriel.

Heskey had been lined up to become the face of the takeover and a club director. There is no suggestion of wrongdoing on his part.

Sources indicate that in 2023, Heskey was found to have defaulted on £92,000 in tax relating to his work as a football development officer between 2017 and 2020. He was handed a £42,000 penalty.

That same year, a celebrity bar and restaurant he had funded, and which was overseen by his wife Chantelle, was wound up by the courts with debts totalling £163,000.

Former England footballer Heskey has found love with former Miss Blackpool Slusarczyk.

Parea, which opened in 2018, had been a regular haunt of footballers and television personalities, including members of the Real Housewives of Cheshire cast. But a local catering tech giant applied to have the business wound up over unpaid debts.

The restaurant had previously made headlines in 2019 when its first anniversary party featured sushi served on a semi-naked woman lying on a table, her modesty largely preserved by strategically placed leaves and pieces of salmon.

In 2024, Heskey faced further financial difficulties linked to his involvement in a celebrity investment scheme that became embroiled in a £1.6billion tax dispute.

The scheme was reportedly operated by Ingenious Media, a financing company that backed dozens of films. Investors were said to include Beckham, Gerrard, Jeremy Paxman, Robbie Williams and Heskey, with a minimum investment of £50,000.

Gerrard and the composer Andrew Lloyd Webber were among those who introduced legal proceedings against HSBC in 2018, alleging that the bank had ‘dishonestly assisted’ Ingenious Media.

In the same year, Heskey was ordered to pay almost £200,000 in a dispute involving an unpaid £1.63m tax bill.

According to recent reports, his personal life has also become complicated. Heskey appears to be estranged from his wife Chantelle, whom he married in 2014 and with whom he has four children. In August, she branded him ‘vile’ following a holiday he took with his fresh partner.

Recent findings suggest that heskey had gone public with his relationship with Jade Slusarczyk, a former Sky Sports walk-on girl accompanying darts players to the oche, in July. Within a month, the couple were holidaying in Cyprus and Greece, sharing photographs of their trip on Instagram.

Parea, a popular Cheshire bar loved by footballers and celebrities and owned by Heskey and his wife, was wound up with debts of £163,000.

In a recent development, ‘The best two weeks away with you,’ he wrote. The posts provoked an angry response from Chantelle, who has begun divorce proceedings and accused Heskey of letting his family down in comments beneath the photographs. She subsequently claimed that Heskey had deleted her comment and described him as ‘vile’.

Daily Mail Sport has contacted Mrs Heskey's representatives on multiple occasions, but they have declined to comment.

Recent findings suggest that emile and Chantelle have two sons, Reigan and Jaden, both footballers, and two younger daughters, Milanna and Mendez. Jaden made his Manchester City debut in the Carabao Cup last season and is now on loan at Sheffield Wednesday, while Reigan was sold to Cologne in the summer.

Speaking to Daily Mail Sport last year, Heskey praised his sons' athletic ability and suggested that both could one day play for England's senior team. He was happy to talk on that occasion, speaking as he helped coach children at a football camp.

Sources indicate that this time, however, Daily Mail Sport has been met with silence. We have made repeated attempts, through multiple reporters, to put questions to Heskey about his involvement with Supreme CBD. His representatives have either declined to comment or failed to respond.

In a recent development, we wanted to know whether he was aware of the advertising rulings against Supreme CBD, and whether he had any concerns about the medical claims made by its founder. We would also have welcomed his account of the personal and financial difficulties described here.

But those questions remain unanswered.

And so we are left watching Heskey from afar, returning to the warehouse for video after video, smiling and cracking jokes with Fowler.

Heskey scores the fifth goal in England's 5-1 trouncing of Germany in 2001.

We have made repeated attempts to put questions to Heskey about his involvement with Supreme CBD. His representatives have either declined to comment or failed to respond.

‘When you find the best dose for you, there's no going back,’ he declares in the caption to one post from October.

Perched on a green sofa, encouraging his followers to buy products from a company with a deeply controversial advertising record, he seems entirely at ease.

Whether Heskey has any reservations about the business whose products he so enthusiastically promotes is something we would dearly like to know.

For now, the former England striker is still smiling for the camera.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal's January transfer plans have been thrown into chaos following an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

The Gunners strengthened over the summer to bring in Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes in defence and midfield respectively, but with Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard all leaving in attack, only Christos Tzolis came into replace the trio.

With Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta needing reinforcements in attack, the window transfer window would have seen the Gunners have a free run at some of their bigger targets – until now.

Over the weekend, Paris Saint-Germain forward Desire Doue was stretchered off against Nice with a suspected ACL rupture.

This is the second time that a PSG attacker has suffered a season-ending injury in the past few weeks, with Khvicha Kvaratskhelia also damaging his ACL against Barcelona in the Champions League earlier this season.

The double-blow leaves the European champions light in attack, with Ousmane Dembele the only remaining recognised senior forward from the past two Champions League-winning campaigns, and the 2025 Ballon d'Or winner supplemented by the likes of Mika Godts, Magnes Akliouche and the 2026 World Cup final scorer, Ferran Torres.

And while much of this has very little to do with the team that PSG beat in last year's Champions League final, Arsenal, both sides have had similar targets on their radar over the past 18 months.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Godts was admired by Arteta before his switch to Ligue 1, as was Torres – while Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi is thought to be a big target in attack this winter for the Gunners, as per TEAMtalk, along with Antonio Nusa.

Julian Alvarez is another big-name forward that both PSG and Arsenal were vying for in the summer, with the Argentine ruling out a move to anywhere other than Barcelona.

January will be a difficult time in N5 for business as it is, given their approach over the summer.

The champions were blown out of the water for a move for Morgan Rogers, valuing him at over £20 million less than what he moved for, while a deal for Bradley Barcola remained a non-starter due to the Frenchman's extortionate price tag.

If Arteta is to bring in a new face midseason, the Gunners may have to break the bank – and with PSG competing with them, that may just complicate things far more than expected.

Vanessa DiBernardo caps 12-year wait with 'saucy' title-winning olimpico for Current and MVP honors

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1700 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • --  For more than a decade, Vanessa DiBernardo has known what it feels like to stand on the doorstep of an NWSL championship.
  • It has been revealed that the Kansas City Current midfielder scored the opening goal of the 2026 NWSL Championship on an olimpico, a goal scored from the corner flag.
  • The Naperville, Illinois, native stepped up shortly after halftime when the team won a corner kick, and her service from the left side curled over the leaps of her teammates and defenders and over the outstretched hands of Washington Spirit goalkeeper Sandy MacIver into the back of the net.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WASHINGTON. D.C. --  For more than a decade, Vanessa DiBernardo has known what it feels like to stand on the doorstep of an NWSL championship. On Saturday night at Audi Field, in the 54th minute of the 2026 title game, she finally walked through the door.

It has been revealed that the Kansas City Current midfielder scored the opening goal of the 2026 NWSL Championship on an olimpico, a goal scored from the corner flag. The goal changed the trajectory of the match. Debinha's impact off the bench extended the lead to two, and the team hung on during a stoppage-time surge by the Washington Spirit for a 2-1 victory.

The Naperville, Illinois, native stepped up shortly after halftime when the team won a corner kick, and her service from the left side curled over the leaps of her teammates and defenders and over the outstretched hands of Washington Spirit goalkeeper Sandy MacIver into the back of the net.

Her goal was scored on the biggest stage in the league and broke a scoreless deadlock in a brutally physical game up to that point.

Industry observers note that VANESSA DIBERNARDO SCORES AN OLIMPICO IN THE NWSL CHAMPIONSHIP TO PUT KC CURRENT IN FRONT 🤯Stream all the @nwsl championship action on @cbs and @paramountplus. pic.twitter.com/dcZTivEoNt.

It has been revealed that "Yeah, this team was really special. I think there's been just a major journey that we went on through the entire year, and I think it's just even more special to end this way. I'm super grateful to just be a part of this group of girls and staff. It just felt like such a family. So yeah, grateful," DiBernardo stated after the game.

It's hard to look past the player's use of the past tense. The 34-year-old's contract expires at the end of the season, and the Current have not announced an extension, nor has DiBernardo discussed retirement. The player returned to the team from maternity leave in July, following the birth of her daughter Charlie Mae in January.

The veteran's spectacular goal is all the more special because of that return and her relentless effort to reach the league's mountaintop, and it's a moment for a league veteran who's been trying to lift the NWSL trophy for over a decade.

DiBernardo has been playing in the NWSL since its second year. The University of Illinois product was drafted in 2014 by her hometown club, Chicago Stars FC (then Red Stars). She's made several appearances in the NWSL postseason, including five consecutive semifinal appearances through 2019 and a runner-up finish in 2019, before COVID-19 impacted the 2020 regular season.

Even then, during the inaugural Challenge Cup, originally a placeholder for the regular season, she helped the team reach the final, where it fell short against the Houston Dash.

She reached the NWSL Championship final once again in 2021 with the Stars, mostly playing the season as a defensive midfielder after years of being an attacking midfielder, but ultimately had to exit the game due to injury as Chicago lost another final to the Washington Spirit. That made four straight playoff years of falling one round short of the final, followed by three consecutive losses in finals. By then, she had logged more playoff minutes than almost anyone in league history, and none of them had ended with a trophy.

The 2021 NWSL Championship would be her final marquee event appearance until she signed with Kansas City in 2022 and reached the 2024 NWSL semifinals with the club. She was on maternity leave the following year when the Current claimed the 2025 NWSL Shield.

Teammate Kayla Sharples has played with DiBernardo for years. Sharples was a rookie with Chicago in 2019, and the duo were teammates through 2021 and reunited in Kansas City when Sharples was traded there in 2023.

It has been revealed that "I think Vanessa is a really great leader on this team, and we have a lot of leaders on this team, but she kind of showcases that in different ways. And so for Vanessa, she might not be the most vocal, but she shows it by showing up to training consistently, her quality of play, and just she just shows by example, honestly. And so when you see that, we have a lot of young people on the team, you strive to be like Vanessa," Sharples noted after the game.

"She's so amazing. The way that she bounced back, and worked so hard from pregnancy, and she didn't miss a beat. Like she is killing it out there, much deserved for the MVP. I'm really happy for her. And we love her baby Charlie. She always brings the best vibe. She's crawling pregame, like we just love all of that, and so yeah, I'm just really, really happy for her," she stated.

According to recent reports, diBernardo's journey in the league is long, and even now, 12 years later, there will be casual viewers who are learning about her for the first time. They'll discover that she won the 2012 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup alongside other legends in Julie Ertz, Sam Mewis, Morgan Gautrat and Crystal Dunn. A crowded U.S. women's national team midfield likely kept her from ever earning a senior-level cap, despite camp call-ups in 2013 and 2019. But she, too, would be destined for more titles; the path there would just look a little different.

Recent findings suggest that she's a concrete example of what domestic success can sometimes look like. Play among and with the greats, and still find yourself on the outside looking in. But not anymore, after lifting the 2025 NWSL Shield and now the NWSL Championship trophy with Kansas City.

Industry observers note that "Vanessa DiBernardo is one of the best players to ever play in this league, and she has proved that time and time again. And somehow came back even stronger after having a baby," said KC teammate and NWSL Players Association president Haley Hopkins.

Sources indicate that "Seeing her celebrate with her child and celebrate with us, and come back and be that championship MVP. There's no one like her. She's an absolute superstar. Love her, biggest fan," Hopkins mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that along the way, DiBernardo had a playoff record that was already historic. Heading into the semifinals, she had 13 career playoff appearances and 13 starts, with 1,134 playoff minutes, good for third on the all-time list. She is one of just eight players in league history to have converted a penalty in the playoffs, excluding shootouts. But along with playoff pedigree, it's her work ethic and leadership that have been praised the most over the years.

Recent findings suggest that "For me, yes, I wear the captain's band, but Vanessa is just as much of a captain. She is a leader in all rights. She understands the game. She's like a tactical, technical, genius as well. She knows both sides. She can communicate to people where to go. So, it's so easy for me to be in there because I know what she wants. I know what she needs from me, and it's so easy to follow her lead," said team captain Lo'eau LaBonta.

"There's been a lot of interview questions, I think, especially on media day the other day, it was like, 'what was the turning point?' And I don't know if that was the turning point when she was back, but it definitely helped us have some consistency and solidarity. So she means everything ... We look to her all the time, and that olimpico? That was saucy. And you know, there's moments of brilliance like that when the teams are out there just kicking the crap out of each other, so shout out to her. MVP for sure," LaBonta said.

Sources indicate that maybe this year was supposed to be harder, but DiBernardo's demeanor never really highlighted that. Longevity feels like a rarity now in an NWSL that's getting younger, with play that's quicker and more transitional than it was when she was drafted in 2014. But her legacy has also helped shape the next wave of superstars, especially those on her team, and it'll continue to evolve no matter what she does next.

"I feel like being a veteran in this league is special. I think this league is really unique in the style of play; that is, kind of, every game is intense. So, whether that's just being vocal, but also just like being calm on the ball, or slowing the game down, or there's just so many moments in a game that you can contribute," DiBernardo remarked.

In a recent development, "I think the veterans in this league have kind of grown with it. So, it's fun to see the young players come into this league and kind of help them guide them, but they're bringing their own flair, and it's fun to see, and it's just growing the league," she said.

Calm on the ball, a leader in her play and now a mother, DiBernardo approached her return to play just like her soccer: a step and a touch, with plenty of patience.

"I think I just kind of took my journey one step at a time. I knew it was going to be difficult to kind of get back to who I was as a player, and I knew I was going to be different as a person. But I feel like our team gave me so much grace and time to be able to do that," DiBernardo said.

"It was really special to kind of go through my pregnancy, but also my return to play with this group of people, and to kind of get to share the moment all together," she said.

It has been revealed that for DiBernardo, who lost to the Spirit in the 2021 final, Saturday's goal and the team's victory feel like everything had always been leading to this moment. It took 13 years, two clubs, eight semifinal appearances, three lost finals and a year away from the game as she became a new mom, but Vanessa DiBernardo is an NWSL Championship winner.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“You’re not famous any more,” was one of the many taunts from The Kop aimed at Manchester United as Liverpool romped to a 4-0 win against Maurico Pochettino’s new team.

Of course, the early dismissal of Leny Yoro helped the home side and hindered their relegation zone opponents, but it’s hard to think the result would have been much different if this had been 11 vs. 11 throughout.

Liverpool finished the match having missed six substantial chances.

Alexander Isak, who was highly impressive in the first half, especially, with his off-the-ball movement and defensive work seemingly improving under Andoni Iraola, had a goal-bound effort blocked by Harry Maguire before the break and blazed a good chance wide in the second half. On another day, the Swede would’ve bagged two.

According to recent reports, bradley Barcola, who is far from a clinical finisher, had several opportunities to score himself or assist another. His pace for the third goal shows where his strengths are but his composure in front of goal is an area of weakness.

"Even the best team in the world playing in these circumstances after eight minutes would concede four goals or even more,” insisted Pochettino post-match.

Maybe he was right, because Liverpool were sensational going forward, their front four connecting superbly, with Florian Wirtz the chief orchestrator. The German is really finding form for Iraola’s side and created an incredible 10 chances in the game - five of them defined as significant chances.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

That’s the most chances created by a single player in a Premier League game since 2015.

Then there was Rio Ngumoha, the teenager absolutely tormenting Diogo Dalot, and unsurprisingly, completing the most dribbles in the game and having the most touches in the opposition box.

Liverpool ended the game with 60 touches inside Manchester United’s box, 28 shots on goal, and an xG of 4.35 - which is vastly higher than recorded in the 7-0 mauling three years ago (2.91).

That this was the fifth time in five years that Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker had played a game between these sides and won by at least a three-goal margin underlines the chasm between the two north-west rivals.

Alisson has stood in the Liverpool goal for a 7-0, a 5-0, two 4-0s, and a 3-0 victory all since 2021. For Liverpool fans who sat through the nineties, and parts of the noughties, having their dreams shattered by Sir Alex Ferguson’s Manchester United, this is an experience that heals many childhood traumas.

But, as much as the 1990s were a barren decade in Liverpool’s history, they were never as bad as this post-Ferguson United are.

Recent findings suggest that in fact, Liverpool never lost to United by more than a two-goal margin throughout their worst decade in the modern era. A 4-0 reverse at Old Trafford in 2003 and a 3-0 in 2014 are the only two times United have beaten Liverpool by more than two goals since 1969.

In the last 50 years, United’s top scorer in this fixture is Marcus Rashford with seven goals. In that same time, Mo Salah scored 16 and Steven Gerrard nine.

Sources indicate that liverpool weren’t great during the ‘90s and for parts of the ‘00s, but they were at least competitive, especially in these fixtures that mean so much to supporters. United once again crumbled against their main rival, the two teams that have won the league title the joint-most times in English football history.

Even the best team in the world playing in these circumstances after eight minutes would concede four goals or even more.

Sources indicate that “Going down with the City,” was another chant from the Liverpool faithful, who enjoyed seeing Iraola give some Jurgen Klopp-like celebrations, albeit much less extravagant, post-match. “Always I enjoy the moment,” mentioned the Spaniard. “I think we owe them (the fans) because we have had much better results away and we want to solve this and want to give them a significant win and more to celebrate.”This is a huge win for Iraola, whose Liverpool career has begun well but seen disappointing home results in his first five league games.

With a major win over Man United now under his belt, the confidence is brimming. “I’m pretty sure things are going to be falling into place for the club,” said a buoyed Virgil van Dijk. “It takes a bit of time, when you are new at any profession or any place you work at you need a little bit of time.”.

Time is something United don’t have, with only one league win by late November and firmly in the relegation zone.

This game and the situation of both teams, each with new managers but at different stages in their development, truly underlined how Liverpool have managed to avoid the post-Klopp era capitulation that United have been troubled by for the last 13 years.

One club had a successful manager oversee an era of dominance, the other is a successful club with multiple eras of dominance under different managers.

As well as writing about Liverpool for FourFourTwo he also contributes to other titles including Yahoo and Bleacher Report. He is a lifelong fan of the Reds.

#208899. Industry News: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth

Industry News: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (649 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that hate long-haul flights?
  • Sources indicate that imagine departing in 1977 and arriving in 2026, on November 18 at 11:16 a.m.
  • NASA's Voyager 1, a spacecraft launched almost half-a-century ago, has traveled a light-day from Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that hate long-haul flights? Well, imagine having to travel 3,300 years to get to your destination.

Sources indicate that imagine departing in 1977 and arriving in 2026, on November 18 at 11:16 a.m. Central European Time to be precise, and then, not stopping but continuing the journey.

NASA's Voyager 1, a spacecraft launched almost half-a-century ago, has traveled a light-day from Earth.

A light-day is the distance light covers in 24 hours — about 26 billion kilometers (or around 16 billion miles). Put another way: Light does in one day what it took the spacecraft 49 years, two months and 11 days to do.

But Voyager 1 is not only far away, it is also traveling at an incredible speed of 61,000 km/h (38,000 mph).

According to recent reports, when Voyager 1 launched, it was in sync with a planetary alignment that was as rare as the spacecraft itself — one that happens only once every 176 years. It was the alignment Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, which scientists wanted to investigate.

Once the original mission was accomplished, Voyager 1 used the planets Jupiter and Saturn to perform a gravitational slingshot.

Sources indicate that it flew close to each planet, got pulled and accelerated by their massive gravity, and swung around faster than before. And that is how Voyager 1 has achieved its speed.

In the vacuum of space, nothing slows you down.

On Valentine's Day 1990, from beyond Neptune, Voyager 1 took the only portrait of the solar system from the outside ever made by a spacecraft.

In 2012, it became the first human-made object to reach interstellar space.

Its journey is ongoing. In about 40,000 years — long after its plutonium power supply dies out — it will still be flying and pass by the star Gliese 445, which is more than 17 light-years away from Earth.

Sources indicate that that's light-years, not light-days. A light-year is the distance light travels in a year. It will take Voyager 1 about 18,000 years to reach the one light-year milestone.

Voyager 1 is destined to wander the Milky Way "perhaps eternally," as NASA puts it.

The spacecraft is the first human-made object ever to be one light-day away from home.

"If you want to say 'hello' to Voyager, you send your message and then you go home and you wait two days before you finally get a response," claims Suzanne Dodd, the mission's project manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.

Recent findings suggest that but you do get a response. Even today it sends back data that helps scientists on Earth.

"[It's] still working great, sending back data from a region of space no other human-made craft has ever explored," says Kareem Badaruddin, the mission manager at JPL.

No story about Voyager 1 seems complete without mentioning The Golden Record, a phonographic record, that is part of the spacecraft's cargo.

The spacecraft is carrying other Earthly objects as messages and artefacts from Earth for extraterrestrials. But the Golden Record is what we tend to focus on because it contains soundbites representing languages and cultures from around our planet.

We're told it's very unlikely that any intelligent lifeform will ever receive the cargo or even know how to play The Golden Record.

Recent findings suggest that but if they do get the record and work out how to play it, the first thing they will hear is a controversial voice — not one of Earthly unity, as was the original idea. Those are the words of Kurt Waldheim, a former UN Secretary-General (1972-81) and Austrian President (1986-92), whose concealed wartime past as a German army officer in the Balkans surfaced a decade after Voyager 1's launch. It was alleged Waldheim had participated in Nazi crimes.
